{"id": "93:4/q09", "question": "How does the promise relate to the preceding denial of abandonment?", "turns_on": "Whether the verse develops the prior honor, explains a revelation pause as approaching death, promises success after present hardship, or gives a circumstantial rationale for non-abandonment.", "positions": [{"id": "93:4/q09/p1", "position": "After reassuring the Prophet of continued revelation and love, God promises a still greater future honor.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Ṭabrisī, al-Rāzī, al-Nasafī, Abū Ḥayyān, al-Bayḍāwī, al-Ālūsī, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī and Bint al-Shāṭiʾ give this ascent; the preceding denial itself confers honor (93:3). Bint al-Shāṭiʾ says verse 5 completes the reassurance. Al-Ālūsī prefers this link to the death proposal; al-Bayḍāwī adds the triumph and elevation of religion among the gifts."}, {"id": "93:4/q09/p2", "position": "A pause in revelation could signal completed mission and imminent death, whose afterlife reward is better.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī distinguishes this from removal from prophethood. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ reports him. Al-Ālūsī calls the proposal much weaker, preferring an independent continuation of reassurance; Elmalılı says immediate death would miss the good of later earthly life (5:3)."}, {"id": "93:4/q09/p3", "position": "The denial answers fears over the present hardship by promising the later success of the mission.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī sees the present hardship changing into victory. Kuran Yolu sets the promise against idolaters' claim that revelation had stopped and the mission would fail. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ reads it as comfort after the pause."}, {"id": "93:4/q09/p4", "position": "The preceding denial is circumstantial: because the Hereafter is better for him, his Lord would not abandon him.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports ʿIṣām al-Dīn's paraphrase, in which the next promise means God will give him the Hereafter; al-Ālūsī objects that the paired lāms and oath make it unlikely and the paraphrase is strained."}]}
{"id": "93:4/q10", "question": "How does the promise fit the sūra's wider movement?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "93:4/q10/p1", "position": "It moves from reassurance and promised future good to reminders of earlier favors and duties arising from them.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī describes day and night as models of developmental trials, then better times, past divine help and obligations. Al-Ṭabrisī links the later reminder of need and gifts to the Giver and future favor. Al-Sāmarrāʾī traces darkness to light through orphanhood and shelter, lostness and guidance, need and wealth. Al-Biqāʿī reports Ibn al-Zubayr's view that a preceding predestination discussion could cause fear, so the sūra reassures God's dearest servant with favors in both lives."}]}
{"id": "93:4/q11", "question": "What event is reported to have preceded this verse's revelation?", "turns_on": "Whether the reported occasion is a vision of the community's later conquests or the pause in revelation and opponents' taunts; Bint al-Shāṭiʾ disputes specifying the pause's cause or length.", "positions": [{"id": "93:4/q11/p1", "position": "The Prophet was shown his community's future conquests, rejoiced, and the verse was revealed.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās transmits this in al-Māwardī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Qurṭubī, al-Suyūṭī, al-Ālūsī and Ibn ʿĀshūr; al-Suyūṭī says al-Ṭabarānī's chain is good. Al-Biqāʿī also reports Anas's account of successive lands opening. Elmalılı calls the foreknowledge a miraculous vision and names Persia, Byzantium and Constantinople as later examples. Al-Ālūsī says the report especially supports the two-abode reading."}, {"id": "93:4/q11/p2", "position": "The sūra answered polytheists who said God had abandoned the Prophet during a pause in revelation.", "reasons": "Al-Bayḍāwī lists proposed causes: an omitted exception formula like 18:23-24, a rebuked questioner, a dead puppy under the bed, or another reason. She dates the sūra to early Mecca, long before the Hijra."}]}
{"id": "93:4/q12", "question": "How many pearl palaces were promised in the reports?", "turns_on": "The reports differ on the number: a thousand versus a million.", "positions": [{"id": "93:4/q12/p1", "position": "A thousand pearl palaces, with spouses and attendants or servants in each.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī adds provisions in each palace. {"id": "93:4/q13", "question": "What other reports and examples illustrate preferring the Hereafter?", "turns_on": "The notes supply separate prophetic reports and sayings rather than rival versions of a single event.", "positions": [{"id": "93:4/q13/p1", "position": "God chose the Hereafter over this world for the Prophet's household.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī transmits Ibn Masʿūd's report of the Prophet's statement."}, {"id": "93:4/q13/p2", "position": "The Prophet compared himself in the world to a rider resting briefly beneath a tree.", "reasons": "Ibn Masʿūd tells of a rough mat marking the Prophet's side; Ibn Kathīr cites al-Tirmidhī's grading of the report as ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ."}, {"id": "93:4/q13/p3", "position": "The Prophet chose to be with God rather than remain alive until the world's end before entering Paradise.", "reasons": "Study Quran reports the choice; Ibn Kathīr also cites the Prophet's choosing what is with God near death as evidence of his asceticism."}, {"id": "93:4/q13/p4", "position": "Al-ʿAbbās inferred from the verse that the Prophet would remain among them only a short time.", "reasons": "Al-Durr reports ʿIkrimah's account of al-ʿAbbās's reaction when the verse was revealed."}, {"id": "93:4/q13/p5", "position": "Both worlds involve hardship, but the more lasting one is worth seeking.", "reasons": "Al-Sulamī reports Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh's counsel."}, {"id": "93:4/q13/p6", "position": "Leaving this world is difficult, but losing the Hereafter is more difficult.", "reasons": "Al-Sulamī reports al-Junayd's comparison."}]}

{"id": "93:4/q15", "question": "What special favor to Muhammad's community is drawn from this comparison?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "93:4/q15/p1", "position": "God's mercy reaches sinners through the obedient, unlike a reported occasion when one sinner kept mercy from Moses's assembly.", "reasons": "Rāzī contrasts Moses's 'with me' (26:62) with Muhammad's 'with us' (9:40), since Abū Bakr was certainly blessed. {"id": "93:4/q16", "question": "What interpretive discipline and early assessments of interpreters are recorded with these notes?", "turns_on": "The notes distinguish standards for claims from reported judgments of particular interpreters; the latter judgments concern different people.", "positions": [{"id": "93:4/q16/p1", "position": "Interpretations must be distinguished by what God alone knows, what the Prophet taught by revelation, and what Arabic usage establishes.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī reserves the Hour and future events to God, calls for sound Prophetic transmission through widespread or reliable reports or clear evidence for revealed explanations, and asks for the clearest proof from circulating Arabic poetry or speech for language-based explanations."}, {"id": "93:4/q16/p2", "position": "Early assessments of individual interpreters diverge.", "reasons": "Al-Shaʿbī sharply rebuked al-Suddī and said a drum beating was preferable to his session; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said al-Suddī interprets according to people's interpretations. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ rejects numerical limits on the verse."}, {"id": "93:5/q08/p6", "position": "It is the Prophet's intercession for his community.", "reasons": "ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and al-Bāqir are cited. {"id": "93:5/q12", "question": "Why do some call this the Qurʾān's most hopeful verse?", "turns_on": "Whether the strongest hope lies in this verse's satisfaction and intercession or 39:53's forgiveness.", "positions": [{"id": "93:5/q12/p1", "position": "The Prophet's household associates it with his concern and intercession for his community.", "reasons": "Reports contrast Iraqis' choice of 39:53 with the household's choice of 93:5; some cite no community member left in the Fire, others intercession for monotheists."}, {"id": "93:5/q12/p2", "position": "Others choose 39:53's promise of forgiveness.", "reasons": "The Iraqis or Qurʾān readers are contrasted with the Prophet's household; Elmalılı interprets 39:53 alongside repentance in 39:54."}]}
